The error `Cannot find module './connectionstate'` on your Render deployment is caused by a case-sensitivity issue between Windows and Linux regarding how the `node_modules` folder was uploaded to your GitHub repository.

### Why this happens
Your local machine runs Windows, which has a **case-insensitive** file system (it sees `connectionState.js` and `connectionstate.js` as the same file). Render uses Linux, which is **case-sensitive**. 

It looks like the `node_modules` folder was committed to your Git repository. Because of the difference in how operating systems handle file capitalization, the `mongoose` module's files got checked into Git with slightly incorrect uppercase/lowercase letters for some files. When Render pulls your code, Node.js strictly looks for `./connectionstate` (all lowercase) and fails because the file might be named `connectionState.js`.

### How to fix it
You should never commit `node_modules` to Git. Instead, Render should install your dependencies fresh using `npm install` on its own Linux environment. 

I've already created a [`.gitignore`](file:///c:/Users/VICTUS/.gemini/.gitignore) file in your project to ignore `node_modules` going forward.

To fix the deployment, please run these commands in your terminal to remove the existing `node_modules` folder from Git and push the changes:

```bash
# 1. Remove node_modules from Git's tracking (this won't delete it from your PC)
git rm -r --cached node_modules
git rm -r --cached API/node_modules

# 2. Commit the changes
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "chore: remove node_modules and add gitignore"

# 3. Push to your repository (this will trigger a new Render deployment)
git push
```

Once you push these changes, Render will build your app and run `npm install` directly on its Linux server, which will download the `mongoose` files with the correct lowercase file names and fix the crash!
